This is ShuttleCoach: a team of AI coaching agents that runs entirely on local hardware.
Here is how it is built, all on one Intel Arc card. The match video becomes 3D shots and match data. Coach agents read it with your memory, test advice in a simulator, and coach you.

Here is what it does. One camera becomes a 3D replay of every rally. Four specialist coaches debate your match at a round table. Ask them by voice, and get highlights ready to post. And between sessions, they stay with you on Telegram.

Drop in match footage: zero bytes leave your machine. The pipeline calibrates the court, isolates the shuttle and lifts every trajectory into 3D. This demo opens a sample match the station has already analysed.

Four coaches read the same match. Coach Lin flashes the zone that cost the most points. Coach Kai grades every shot from its 3D flight. Coach Ren shows which muscles to train, and adapts to a sore knee. Coach Ada finds the opponent's habits under pressure.

Like real coaches, they disagree, and each one speaks live from the local model. Lin wants smash-defence blocks; Ren says the knee is sore. The head coach rules: health first, then the points at stake, and writes four measurable goals and a seven-day plan. Ask any coach a question: a local model answers in about a second, and a verifier checks every number before you see it.

And they keep learning. Every night a research agent reads new sports-science papers, and each coach proposes changes to its own playbook. But AI that learns must be AI you can trust. Every change must cite a study, pass a safety check and do no harm on its tests. Anything about health waits for a human coach. So this one is declined.

Off the court, the same staff lives in Telegram. Coach Mei plans meals from what is in your kitchen, and the bot checks in after the session to log it. Say you want a game. The agent opens the map, finds where everyone starts, checks every sports centre, and picks the court that is fairest for everyone's trip. It invites your friends, and books only when you confirm.

Here is the agent behind it. The local model reads the request. The agent checks each player's calendar and where they start, searches the sports centres for a free court, and ranks them by the longest trip anyone would make. Then it books the court on the venue's own website, the way a person would, and stops before the final confirm until you say yes. Every step is logged on the station.
No cloud and no upload, built for a single Intel Arc Pro B70 workstation. ShuttleCoach: a private staff of AI agents that evolves with you, and never leaves your court.
